images.title: A rhombus from diagonals 4 cm and 5 cm
images.purpose: Shows the rhombus built from diagonals of 5 cm and 4 cm that bisect each other at right angles.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two crossing diagonals at right angles in the centre with their ends joined into a rhombus.
images.exact_structure: Two straight segments crossing at their midpoint O at right angles: AC is a thick teal (#0072B2) horizontal line and BD is a thick amber (#E69F00) vertical line, a little shorter. A small filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) square right angle mark at O. Each half of AC is labelled 2.5 cm and each half of BD is labelled 2 cm. The four ends are joined in order A, B, C, D by thin dashed grey (#6B7280) lines, making a rhombus standing on a corner; each side carries one identical short tick mark. The letters A, B, C, D sit just outside the four ends, A at the left, B at the top, C at the right, D at the bottom. No side lengths. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Diagonals that bisect each other at right angles always give a rhombus.
images.description: Shows the rhombus built from diagonals of 5 cm and 4 cm that bisect each other at right angles.
images.context: Halves 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5 cm and 4 ÷ 2 = 2 cm, crossing at 90°.

image_decisions.why: The construction this practice asks for, shown in its finished simplest state.
